response.text:
Recent work supports separating sampling failure from representation failure. [Evaluating Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds that aggregate accuracy hides head/mid/tail disparities: random negatives favor popular items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost. [gSASRec (2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) identifies overconfidence induced by negative-sampled BCE; [rank-estimation research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) examines correcting sampling bias. These motivate measuring per-example gradient norms, positive/negative contributions and saturation rates across training-derived popularity and history-length strata, rather than relying only on score margins.

[Long-Sequence Recommendation Models Need Decoupled Embeddings (ICLR 2025)](https://ise.thss.tsinghua.edu.cn/~mlong/doc/Long-Sequence-Recommendation-ICLR25.pdf) directly measures conflicting embedding gradients from attention and representation modules, finding both directional disagreement and magnitude domination; simple projections do not reliably resolve the conflict. This is attention-specific evidence, not an established NextItNet failure. For NextItNet, a proposed adaptation is layerwise cosine agreement between stratum gradients, their norms and cancellation ratios, alongside activation effective rank. Near-zero negative gradients suggest easy-negative saturation; persistent disagreement suggests competing signals; low rank alone cannot establish a bottleneck.

Calibrate these hypotheses with bounded, separately evaluated interventions within one NextItNet per category: modest semi-hard negative sampling, capped stratum reweighting, or a width/residual-path adjustment. Compare diagnostic changes and pinned macro validation HR@10 under fixed seeds and budget. Training-gradient improvements cannot establish held-out ranking gains; retain final-position readout for left-padded histories and one checkpoint per category.
